name: Missouri

regulator.name: Missouri Office of Athlete Agents (Division of Professional Registration)

law.name: Revised Uniform Athlete Agents Act (RSMo 436.215 and following)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. RSMo 173.280 says only attorneys or agents licensed by Missouri may represent college athletes for NIL.
summary: Register with the Office of Athlete Agents. $102 with fingerprints. Expires June 30 of odd years.
contract_warning: Warning to student athlete. If you sign this contract: (1) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport; (2) both you and your athlete agent are required to tell your athletic director, if you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after entering into an agency contract or before the next athletic event in which you participate, whichever occurs first, and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent; and (3) you may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of the contract may not reinstate your eligibility.

steps.text: Fill out the Application for Athlete Agent Registration
steps.detail: Attach 2 photos and proof of citizenship.

steps.text: Get fingerprinted
steps.detail: Attach 2 fingerprint cards.

steps.text: Pay $102
steps.detail: $70 application + $20 state check + $12 FBI check. Payable to Missouri Office of Athlete Agents.

steps.text: Mail it to the Office of Athlete Agents
steps.detail: 3605 Missouri Blvd., P.O. Box 1335, Jefferson City, MO 65102.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: Tell every school where the athlete is enrolled. If the athlete reached out first, tell them within 10 days.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Say you are registered in Missouri. Include your pay and how it's figured, anyone not on your application who gets paid, expenses the athlete pays back, your services, how long it lasts and the date signed.

steps.text: For NIL work, spell out each side's duties and your fees in the contract
steps.detail: Missouri's NIL law says the deal must be in writing and signed by you both.

steps.text: Make sure the athlete shows their school your contract before signing
steps.detail: Missouri's NIL law says a college athlete must disclose a representation contract to the school before it is signed.

steps.text: Put the warning to student athlete box next to the athlete's signature
steps.detail: Bold capital letters. Use the words from Missouri law. If the athlete is a minor, a parent or guardian signs and the warning is reworded for them.

steps.text: Have the athlete sign a separate eligibility warning
steps.detail: It says signing may cost them their eligibility. A parent or guardian signs instead if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy when they sign
steps.detail: Give it to a parent or guardian if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Notify the athletic director within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Do it in writing, or before the athlete's next scheduled game if that comes first. The athlete must tell them too, with your name and contact info.

steps.text: Let the athlete cancel within 14 days if they want
steps.detail: They cancel by telling you in writing. They owe you nothing and keep anything you gave them. This right can't be waived.

steps.text: If the athlete enrolls at a school later, tell that athletic director within 72 hours
steps.detail: The clock starts when you knew or should have known they enrolled.

steps.text: If you knew the athlete before they got an athletic scholarship, tell the school within 10 days of enrolling
steps.detail: This applies if you recruited them, or the relationship was meant to lead to a contract.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Federal law (SPARTA) bans pre-dating or post-dating it.

steps.text: Keep client records for 5 years
steps.detail: Names and addresses, every contract and your recruiting costs. The state can inspect them during business hours.

steps.text: If you give an athlete anything that could cost their eligibility, tell the athletic director within 72 hours
steps.detail: The athlete must also sign a record saying it may cost them their eligibility. Without both, the gift is not allowed.

steps.text: Never give false info to get an athlete to sign, or pre-date or post-date a contract
steps.detail: Don't get anyone else to break these rules for you either.

steps.text: Renew by June 30 of each odd year and pay $70
steps.detail: The renewal fee is $70. The next renewal is June 30, 2027.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: The June 30 odd-year expiration comes from the application form (MO 375-0235, 2-2025). The statute section on the registration term was not read.
Missouri's NIL law (RSMo 173.280) was last changed in 2023 on the Revisor site. Check for 2025 or 2026 changes at https://revisor.mo.gov.
The criminal and civil penalty sections were not reviewed.
